source_text.body:
Update a website and order food by delegating to an agent
A reviewer gave Dots computer access; it updated a website from voice notes, assembled a video, and ordered teriyaki after login help, but missed the free coworking option.
·
Oct 2, 2026
Done with
DO
Dots
What they did
The reviewer gave Dots access to her computer with broad permissions. For the website, she spent 10 minutes describing changes by voice, and Dots redesigned and deployed an update. It also assembled local video files into a social-media clip. For errands, a person handled a human check and helped it log in to Uber Eats.
How it went
The website and video tasks worked. Dots placed a teriyaki order after login help. It offered a $35 coworking pass instead of the free option, and an IKEA security check kept looping.
Worth knowing
Dots worked better on the reviewer's own files and site than on third-party sites, where security checks stalled it. OpenAI advises reviewing consequential work.
Try it yourself
with
Dots
Copy prompt
Use your computer to help me with these tasks: [update the page at my website URL using the notes I'll paste or dictate] and [order lunch from my usual restaurant for delivery to my address]. If you need me to log in, ask and wait. Before publishing any website change or placing any order, show me exactly what you are about to do and the total cost, and wait for my approval. Before ordering, also check for free or cheaper alternatives like [a free coworking pass or a lunch deal] and tell me what you found.
Original source: https://www.neoteo.com/en/openai-dots-review-website-and-video-tasks-worked-online-errands-hit-snags
